facts.text: A Monte Carlo method answers a question by running the same experiment many times with randomly chosen inputs and counting the outcomes.
facts.quote: A Monte Carlo method answers a question by running the same experiment many times with randomly chosen inputs and counting what happens.

facts.text: In Monte Carlo simulation, each run randomly draws parameters such as speed, distance, dust and a person's path from the scenario family's probability distribution and records the outcome.
facts.quote: In simulation, each run draws its parameters (speed, distance, dust, the person's path) at random from the scenario family's probability distribution, and the outcome is recorded.

facts.text: After many Monte Carlo simulation runs, the fraction of misses estimates the miss rate.
facts.quote: After many runs, the fraction of misses estimates the miss rate.

facts.text: The booklet's estimation stream uses a Monte Carlo campaign on a frozen sample.
facts.quote: The booklet's estimation stream is a Monte Carlo campaign on a frozen sample.

facts.text: Aircraft collision-avoidance logic ACAS X was evaluated using encounter-model Monte Carlo runs equivalent to billions of flight hours.
facts.quote: Chapter 2 notes that aircraft collision-avoidance logic (ACAS X) was evaluated with encounter-model Monte Carlo runs equivalent to "billions of flight hours" [Chapter 2].

facts.text: If the true miss rate is one in 10,000, a plain Monte Carlo campaign sees about one miss per 10,000 runs and needs tens of thousands of runs to obtain enough misses for a precise estimate.
facts.quote: If the true miss rate is one in 10,000, a plain Monte Carlo campaign sees about one miss per 10,000 runs and needs tens of thousands of runs before it has seen enough misses to say anything precise.

facts.text: The booklet concludes that pure Monte Carlo is extremely inefficient for rare dangerous events.
facts.quote: The booklet states that pure Monte Carlo is "extremely inefficient for rare dangerous events"

facts.text: The booklet's planning chapter concludes that naive Monte Carlo cannot reach low failure rates in four months.
facts.quote: in the planning chapter, that naive Monte Carlo cannot reach low failure rates in four months [Chapter 9, Chapter 12].

facts.text: The booklet recommends Monte Carlo as the honest default for estimating rates.
facts.quote: Monte Carlo is the honest default for estimating rates

facts.text: Monte Carlo's need for many runs motivates the booklet's sample-size tables and rare-event methods.
